idiom_name: Sidekiq Dead set (retry: 0 / sidekiq_retry_in returning :kill / sidekiq_retries_exhausted)
implementation_notes: Sidekiq has no decode step of its own, so an invalid payload surfaces as an argument or schema validation failure inside perform and the Dead set is the invalid channel. Two documented paths lead there: sidekiq_options retry: 0 sends a failed job straight to the Dead set without burning the usual 25 retries, and the sidekiq_retry_in hook can return :kill for the exception class that means 'this job can never succeed'. sidekiq_retries_exhausted and the global death_handlers fire just before the move, which is where alerting or an external error store hooks in - Sidekiq's own guidance is explicit that retries are for unexpected errors, so validation failures belong on the dead path.
code_sketch:
class IngestJob
  include Sidekiq::Job
  sidekiq_options retry: 0, backtrace: 5   # invalid payloads: straight to Dead set

  def perform(payload)
    raise InvalidPayload, 'schema mismatch' unless SCHEMA.valid?(payload)
    Ingest.call(payload)
  end
end
pitfalls: retry: false discards the job entirely whereas retry: 0 keeps it in the Dead set; choosing the wrong one turns the invalid channel into a black hole.
The Dead set is bounded (by default 10,000 jobs or six months) and Sidekiq discards beyond that, so the invalid channel still needs a drain or export path.
The job hash is already re-serialized JSON by the time the job runs; framing-level corruption must be captured at the queue or HTTP boundary, not inside the worker.
